name: Field_ActorGimmick_UpdateModel
summary: Thin per-frame override of a field actor-gimmick class: it forwards straight to the base actor model update (0x0018233C) without touching any own field. It exists only to occupy the model-update slot of the gimmick class's method table (0x0075FB3C, entry +0x28), which also holds maybe_Field_ActorGimmick_AddTriggerCommand (0x002BED50) and maybe_Field_ActorGimmick_UpdateActEffect (0x002BE754).
evidence: Disassembly at 0x002BE7D8 is exactly `push {r4,lr}; bl 0x18233C; pop {r4,pc}` (12 bytes, r0 untouched), and 0x18233C is the named caller/callee maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateModel: handle resolve, vtable +0xD0 step, ground/effect offset per model kind, animation transform and collision position. The entry sits at offset +0x28 of the actor-gimmick method table 0x0075FB3C together with the other maybe_Field_ActorGimmick_* entries, so the first-pass guess is supported and is only a forwarding override.

name: Field_ActorGimmick_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the field actor-gimmick class: installs the class descriptor at 0x0075FB34 (whose entry table starts at 0x0075FB3C), destroys the embedded Ui_Object at +0x38C, runs the base class destructor body (handle release + member teardown) and finally frees the object. The 4-byte prologue at 0x002BEDF0 (`ldr r1,=0x0075FB34`) is the real table entry; Ghidra started the recovered function one instruction later.
evidence: The constructor at 0x002BEDA8 stores the same descriptor (literal 0x0075FB34 at 0x002BEDEC) into the new object and initialises the mesh at +0x38C with 0x00591DE8 Field_Object2D_InitMesh, so this is that class's destructor. Body: store the descriptor, 0x004D714C (a thunk to 0x0017C334 Ui_Object_DtorBody) on self+0x38C, 0x00184CB4 (the Field_Object destructor body, which installs 0x007588B4 and tears down the embedded objects) on self, then the universal delete tail 0x0010F6CC. Old name only said Dtor; the assembly shows the free tail, so DeletingDtor.

name: Ui_Window_DeletingDtorD
summary: Deleting destructor of a Ui window class: it calls the base Ui widget destructor body (0x001D8C2C installs the base table 0x0075A3F4, unlinks the two intrusive lists at +0xD4/+0x114, releases the 3-D scene node, then unlinks the second list pair) and frees the object. The concrete window class is not identifiable from the data, so it takes the next free letter suffix after the three Ui_Window_DeletingDtorA/B/C entries.
evidence: Body is exactly `push {r4,lr}; bl 0x001D8C2C; pop {r4,lr}; b 0x0010F6CC` (0x0010F6CC is the operator-delete tail used by every deleting destructor in the tree). The class table 0x0075FC14 starts with this entry and continues with 0x001D863C/0x001D8718/0x001D8630/0x001D86E8/0x001D89B4 Ui_Window_LayoutRows/0x002BEE1C maybe_Ui_Window_LayoutRowsSimple/0x001D8A80 Ui_Widget_ApplyScreenTransform/0x001D86C8; the base table 0x0075A3F4 holds that same method sequence after its own dtor pair 0x001D8C2C + 0x001D8BD0, which pins this as a derived Ui window class. That is more specific than the old 'Widget' wording, and the 'E' suffix carried no information.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_ApplyDrawEntryFragment
summary: Not an independent function: this is the fall-through tail of the method whose real entry is 0x002BEEF8 (slot 4 of the actor-action method table 0x0075FC64). When the move-parameter flag byte at +0x48 (copied from actor+0x25C) is non-zero, the combined method reads the shared drawing-table entry value (0x0029E488: graphics context +0xF50, default row, style 10) and stores its low byte into the actor model node at f_28->f_B8->+0x128.
evidence: Disassembly proves the fall-through: 0x002BEEF8 is `ldrb r1,[r0,#0x48]; cmp r1,#0; bxeq lr` (returns early) and then continues straight into 0x002BEF04 (`push {r4,lr}; ldr r4,[r0,#0x28]; bl 0x0029E488; ldr r1,[r4,#0xB8]; strbne r0,[r1,#0x128]`), so the guard is the first half of the same routine and 0x002BEF04 is not a callable entry. The old name's 'frame index' is not supported: 0x0029E488 forces index=-1/style=10/mode=2 into 0x0029E498, which is the same shared-table byte lookup that the named sprite factories (Gfx_Sprite2D_InitFromDesc, Field_CreateActor) feed into model+0x128; the field's exact meaning stays a hypothesis, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Actor_Action_DtorDeleteA
summary: Deleting destructor of an actor-action class: calls the shared actor-action destructor body (0x00294C24 is a 4-byte branch to 0x00193E44, which re-installs the base descriptor 0x00758AE0) and then frees the object. The concrete action class (the table 0x0075FC64 also holds Actor_SyncFacingToTarget and the curve-move Begin/ApplyPosition pair) cannot be named from the data, so the A suffix stays.
evidence: Exact assembly `push {r4,lr}; bl 0x00294C24; pop {r4,lr}; b 0x0010F6CC`, and 0x00294C24 is the tail-branch alias of 0x00193E44 (`ldr r1,=0x00758AE0; str r1,[r0]; bx lr`). The entry is slot 0 of the method table 0x0075FC64 (0x002BEF20 Actor_SyncFacingToTarget, 0x00294BD0 Actor_Action_InitDescriptor, 0x002BEFEC/0x002BEFC0 curve-move pair, 0x002BEEF8). Corroborates the previous deleting-destructor guess; the name is kept word for word.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_ApplyDrawEntryFragmentB
summary: Not an independent function: the fall-through tail of the method whose real entry is 0x002BF1D8 (slot 4 of the actor-action method table 0x0075FC98). The combined method first requires the action state byte at +0x2C to be non-zero and the move-flag byte at +0x48 to be set, then copies the shared drawing-table entry byte (0x0029E488) into actor model f_B8->+0x128 - the same body as 0x002BEF04.
evidence: 0x002BF1D8 is `ldrb r1,[r0,#0x2C]; cmp r1,#0; ldrbne r1,[r0,#0x48]; cmpne r1,#0; bxeq lr` and falls straight into 0x002BF1EC, whose emitted C is byte-identical to 0x002BEF04. It is therefore a shared tail block guarded by the action state, not a second 'apply frame' entry - the previous name double-counted one routine. 0x002BF208 (same table, slot 1) shows +0x48 is the flag byte copied from actor+0x25C and +0x2C is the state byte, which supports the guard reading.

name: Actor_Action_CopyMoveParams
summary: Begin/setup step of a curve-move actor action: snapshots the owning actor's move parameter block (actor+0x244..+0x258, six dwords, plus the flag byte at +0x25C) into the action's own fields +0x30..+0x48 and clears the state byte at +0x2C to 0 so the action starts in its initial state.
evidence: Disassembly confirms the field-for-field copy: `ldr r0,[r0,#0x28]; add r0,r0,#0x244` then six `ldr/str` pairs to self+0x30..+0x44, `ldrb r0,[r0,#0x18]` / `strb r0,[r4,#0x18]` (actor+0x25C -> self+0x48) and finally `strb r0,[r5,#0x2C]` with r0=0. It is slot 1 (the begin slot) of the method table 0x0075FC98 whose later slots are the curve-move Update/ApplyPosition pair, matching the old 'move params' guess; the old summary wrongly called +0x2C an animator pointer - it is the state byte compared with 0..4 by 0x002BF298/0x002BF5C4.

name: Actor_Action_DtorDeleteB
summary: Deleting destructor of a second actor-action class: calls the same shared actor-action destructor body (0x00294C24 -> 0x00193E44) and frees the object. Its method table 0x0075FC98 is the curve-move variant whose Update/ApplyPosition slots are 0x002BF298/0x002BF260, but no class name is recoverable from the data, so the B suffix stays.
evidence: Exact assembly `push {r4,lr}; bl 0x00294C24; pop {r4,lr}; b 0x0010F6CC`; entry 0 of the method table 0x0075FC98, which is followed immediately by 0x002BF208 (CopyMoveParams), 0x00294BD0 Actor_Action_InitDescriptor, 0x002BF298 maybe_Actor_Action_CurveMove2_Update, 0x002BF1D8 and 0x002BF260 maybe_Actor_Action_CurveMove2_ApplyPosition - i.e. the same shape as 0x002BF1C8 one table earlier. Confirms the deleting-destructor reading; the name is kept word for word.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_Move_UpdateFragment
summary: Ghidra-split fragment, not a factory: 0x002BFA68 itself is only the four-byte `b 0x0022CECC (Actor_TrySelectIdleAnimation)` tail that ends the state==2 path of Actor_Action_Move_Update (0x002BF9F4) after it stores the state byte 3; the 620-byte body Ghidra attached here is the state==0/1 half of that same update state machine (0x002BFA6C..0x002BFCD0), including the timing calculations 0x004239C0/0x0042383C/0x00423950, the scratch buffer alloc (0x0011CFAC + 0x00116AE0 + 0x0010B2C4 Anim_Sequence_CtorBase) and SE 0x53.
evidence: The instruction at 0x002BFA68 is `b #0x22cecc`, reached only after the epilogue `vpop {d8}; pop {r4,r5,r6,r7,r8,lr}` at 0x002BFA5C-0x002BFA64 that belongs to 0x002BF9F4 (maybe_Actor_Action_Move_Update, 116 bytes in the Ghidra index). 0x002BF9F4 branches forward to 0x002BFA6C (`beq #0x2bfa6c` at 0x002BFA24), so the whole 0x002BFA6C..0x002BFCD0 range is the continuation of Move_Update and the next real entry is 0x002BFCD4 Actor_Action_Move_Finish. The previous name CreateMoveSequence described that mis-attributed body, so it is wrong for this address; the level of certainty about the split keeps it at maybe_.

name: Actor_Action_Move_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the actor move action: runs the shared actor-action destructor body (0x00294C24 -> 0x00193E44, which restores the base descriptor 0x00758AE0) and frees the object.
evidence: Exact assembly `push {r4,lr}; bl 0x00294C24; pop {r4,lr}; b 0x0010F6CC`. It is entry 0 of the move-action method table 0x0075FCCC whose remaining slots are 0x002BF760 Move_Setup, 0x002BFCD4 Actor_Action_Move_Finish, 0x002BF9F4 Move_Update, 0x002BF5C4 Move_ApplyShadowHeightToActors and 0x002BF884 Move_UpdateObjectExtent - so the class hint 'Move' is solid and only the naming style changed.

name: Actor_Action_Move_RestorePosition
summary: Ends the move/landing step: first calls the actor through virtual slot +0x88 (r0 = actor, result discarded - the per-step motion/transform hook), then copies the saved landing position actor+0x3AC/+0x3B0/+0x3B4 back into the live position +0x9C/+0xA0/+0xA4 and marks the transform dirty (+0x118 = 1) so the node is rebuilt next frame.
evidence: Disassembly at 0x002BFEE8: `ldr r0,[r0,#0x28]; ldr r1,[r0]; ldr r1,[r1,#0x88]; blx r1` then `ldr/str` of +0x3AC/+0x3B0/+0x3B4 into +0x9C/+0xA0/+0xA4 and `mov r1,#1; strb r1,[r0,#0x118]`. The neighbouring entry 0x002BFF64 does exactly the same copy/dirty sequence without the virtual call, which isolates the call as the 'apply motion first' half - the old summary already had this reading; the new disassembly only makes it exact, hence confirmed.

name: Actor_Action_Move_UpdateAnimStep0
summary: Drives the move action's animator one step: takes the animator handle at +0x2C, calls its slot +0x14 with (&handle, 0), and only if that reports progress calls slot +0x10 on the same handle (tail call). This is the per-frame animation step of the move action, distinct from the state-machine update in 0x002BF9F4.
evidence: Disassembly at 0x002BFF28: `add r4,r0,#0x2c; ldr r0,[r0,#0x2c]; mov r1,#0; ldr r2,[r0,#0x14]; mov r0,r4; blx r2; cmp r0,#0; beq end; ldr r0,[r4]; ldr r1,[r0,#0x10]; mov r0,r4; pop {r4,lr}; bx r1`. It is slot 1 of the animator-driver method table 0x0075FD00 together with 0x002C0704 Actor_Action_Detach and 0x002C0654 Move_UpdateAnimation. 'Step0' is the literal argument 0 passed to slot +0x14, which matches the old reading; the exact call chain is new.
